  WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                §     ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS

                  APPLICANTS’ PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT,
               CONCLUSIONS OF LAW, AND ORDERING PARAGRAPHS

        These proposed findings of fact, conclusions of law, and ordering paragraphs address the

joint application of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation to amend their certificates of convenience and necessity for the Bell County East

Switch to Big Hill Substation 765 kilovolt transmission line project in Bell, Burnet, Concho,

Coryell, Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom

Green, and Williamson counties, Texas (Project).


                          I.     PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT

Joint Applicants
   1.      Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (Oncor) is a Delaware limited liability
           company registered with the Texas secretary of state under filing number 800880712.

   2.      Oncor owns and operates for compensation in Texas facilities and equipment to
           transmit and distribute electricity in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc.
           (ERCOT) region.

   3.      Oncor holds certificate of convenience and necessity (CCN) number 30043 to provide
           service to the public.

                                                1
                                          Proposed Order
                        SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
    4.     LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (LCRA TSC) is a Texas non-profit
          corporation registered with the Texas secretary of state under filing number
          159084801.

   5.     LCRA TSC owns and operates facilities to transmit electricity in the ERCOT region.

   6.     LCRA TSC provides service under CCN number 30110.

Joint Application
   7.     On March 26, 2026, Oncor and LCRA TSC (Applicants) filed an application
          (Application) with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) to amend
          their CCNs to (1) expand Oncor’s Bell County East Switch to include a 765 kilovolt
          (kV) switchyard, (2) develop a 765 kV transmission line running from LCRA TSC’s
          Big Hill Substation to Oncor’s Bell County East Switch, and (3) construct
          telecommunication facilities, including fiber repeater huts, for the operation of the line.

   8.     Applicants hired Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. (Kimley-Horn) and Halff
          Associates, Inc. (Halff) to prepare an environmental assessment and routing study (EA)
          for the proposed transmission line, which was included as part of the Application.

   9.     On April 20, 2026, Commission staff (Staff) recommended that the Application be
          found sufficient.

   10.    In State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) Order No. 7, issued on April 21,
          2026, the administrative law judges (ALJs) found the Application sufficient.

Description of the Transmission Facilities
   11.    Applicants propose to construct, own, and operate a new, single-circuit 765-kV
          transmission line between the expansion at Oncor’s Bell County East Switch and
          LCRA TSC’s Big Hill Substation. In addition to the transmission line, proposed
          transmission facilities include Oncor’s construction of a new 765-kV switchyard at Bell
          County East Switch and the telecommunications facilities needed to operate the line.

   12.    Oncor’s Bell County East Switch is located 5.5 miles southeast of the city of Temple
          in Bell County.

   13.    LCRA TSC’s Big Hill Substation is located approximately 13 miles northeast of the
          City of Eldorado in Schleicher County.

   14.    Except where alternative structures and/or a different right-of-way width is required
          due to design, construction, or other engineering-related constraints, the proposed 765
          kV transmission line will be constructed on single-circuit self-supporting steel lattice
          towers, generally within a 200-foot right-of-way.

   15.    The typical structure will be between approximately 155 and 160 feet in height for
          Oncor’s portion of the transmission line, and between approximately 140-170 feet in
          height for LCRA TSC’s portion of the transmission line, although the actual height
                                               2
                                         Proposed Order
                       SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
                may vary depending on terrain and other engineering-related constraints. The
               estimated maximum height for the typical structure will be approximately 198 feet.

Description of the Proposed Routes
      16.      Applicants’ Application included 122 alternative routes for the Commission’s
               consideration that meet the certification requirements of PURA 1 and the Commission’s
               substantive rules. 2

      17.      All filed routes are viable and constructible.

      18.      Applicants identified alternative Route 894, which is approximately 223.7 miles in
               length and consists of route links A0, A1, A2, B1, B21, C4, D12, C5, E52, F1, F31,
               F32, F20, F23, G72, G73, G82, G13, G51, G52, H1, H41, H42, J21, J22, J23, J27, J4,
               K11, K7, J16, K13, K51, K52, M11, M12, N3, P2, R1, T1, T2, and Z2 as the route that
               best addresses the applicable routing factors of PURA and the Commission’s rules.

      19.      Staff identified Route 487 as the route that best addresses the applicable routing factors.

Schedule

      20.      In the Application, Oncor estimated that it would acquire all right-of-way by September
               2027, finalize engineering and design by July 2028, procure material and equipment by
               May 2030, complete construction by December 2030, and energize the proposed
               transmission facilities by December 2030. LCRA TSC estimated that it would acquire
               all right-of-way by August 2028, finalize engineering and design by November 2028,
               procure material and equipment by March 2029, complete construction by December
               2030, and energize the proposed transmission facilities by December 2030.
               Applicants’ estimates were premised on the Commission’s approval of the Application
               within 180 days of the Application’s filing.

Public Input
      21.      On January 24, 2025, Kimley-Horn and Halff mailed consultation letters to various
               public officials and agencies informing them of the proposed transmission facilities and
               giving them an opportunity to provide information about the proposed transmission
               facilities and general Project area. In response, Applicants, Kimley-Horn, and Halff
               received information from various public officials and agencies.

      22.      To develop information on community values for the transmission facilities, Applicants
               held three public participation meetings at the following locations on the identified
               dates: (1) Salado ISD Meadows Room in Salado, Texas on June 16, 2025; (2) Lampasas
               ISD Old Middle School Cafeteria in Lampasas, Texas on June 17, 2025; and (3)
               Menard County Community Center in Menard, Texas on June 18, 2025.

          participation meetings to all owners of property located within 520 feet of the
          centerlines of the preliminary alternative route links for the Project. The notice
          included details of the public meetings, a map of the study area depicting the
          preliminary routes, and additional information about the proposed transmission line.

   24.    Applicants sent notice of the public participation meetings to the Department of
          Defense Siting Clearinghouse (now known as the Military Aviation and Installation
          Assurance Siting Clearinghouse) via email and mail.

   25.    Notice of the public participation meetings was published on June 10, 2025, in Temple
          Daily Telegram, a newspaper of general circulation in Bell County, Lampasas Dispatch
          Record, a newspaper of general circulation in Lampasas County, and San Angelo
          Standard-Times, a newspaper of general circulation in Tom Green County; on June 11,
          2025, in Burnet Bulletin, a newspaper of general circulation in Burnet County, Mason
          County News, a newspaper of general circulation in Mason County, Brady-Standard
          Herald, a newspaper of general circulation in McCulloch County, and Georgetown-
          Williamson County Sun, a newspaper of general circulation in Williamson County; and
          on June 12, 2025, in Eden Echo, a newspaper of general circulation in Concho County,
          Menard News and Messenger, a newspaper of general circulation in Menard County,
          San Saba News & Star, a newspaper of general circulation in San Saba County, and
          Eldorado Success, a newspaper of general circulation in Schleicher County.

   26.    A total of 825 individuals signed in as attendees at the public participation meetings.

   27.    A total of 189 questionnaires were received by Applicants, Halff, and Kimley-Horn at
          the public participation meetings, and numerous questionnaires and other
          correspondence were received following the meetings via mail, email, or phone.

   28.    Based on the information gathered through the public participation meetings, additional
          field and aerial investigations by Halff, Kimley-Horn and Applicants, and guidance
          from Applicants, Halff and Kimley-Horn made several modifications to the
          preliminary route links.

             Mason, McCulloch, Menard, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, Williamson, Mills,
             Milam, Coryell, and Llano counties, Texas;

30.   On March 26, 2026, Applicants sent a copy of the Application and all attachments,
      including the EA, to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department (TPWD) by overnight
      mail delivery.

31.   On March 31, 2026, Applicants published notice of the Application in Lampasas
      Dispatch Record; on April 1, 2026, in Temple Daily Telegram, Burnet Bulletin, Mason
      County News, Brady-Standard Herald, Goldthwaite Eagle, San Angelo Standard-

      Press the week of April 13, 2026, and the Burnet Bulletin the week of April 20, 2026.
      Together, these sixteen newspapers have general circulation in the Texas counties
      where the certificate is being requested.

Referral to SOAH for Hearing
    36.     On March 30, 2026, the Commission referred this docket to SOAH and issued a
            preliminary order that, among other things, established a decision deadline and
            specified issues to be addressed in this proceeding.

    37.     In SOAH Order No. 1, filed on March 31, 2026, the SOAH ALJs scheduled a
            prehearing conference via Zoom videoconference for April 14, 2026.

    38.     At the prehearing conference on April 14, 2026, the parties agreed to a procedural
            schedule, which was subsequently filed by Applicants on April 15, 2026.

    39.     In SOAH Order No. 6, filed on April 20, 2026, the SOAH ALJs memorialized the
            prehearing conference and adopted the proposed procedural schedule. The procedural
            schedule set the hearing on the merits to begin the afternoon of June 8, 2026, and
            continue through June 12, 2026.

    40.     In SOAH Order No. 15, filed on May 18, 2026, the SOAH ALJs amended the schedule
            by moving the prehearing conference to the afternoon of June 5, 2026, and setting the
            hearing on the merits to begin the morning of June 8, 2026, and continue through June
            12, 2026.

Need for the Project
   70.    The proposed transmission facilities are needed to address rapid load growth and help
          ensure the availability of reliable transmission service in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell,
          Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher,
          Tom Green, and Williamson counties and surrounding areas.

   71.    The proposed Project will establish a new 765-kV transmission pathway that will work
          in conjunction with related upgrades to enhance Applicants’ load-serving capability in
          the area.

    72.     On April 24, 2025, the Commission approved the 765 kV import paths identified in the
           Permian Basin Reliability Plan and authorized the applicable TSPs to file CCN
           applications for the necessary 765 kV import path projects, as identified by ERCOT.

   73.     The Permian Basin Reliability Plan defined each of the three 765 kV import paths that
           are needed to reliably serve the Permian Basin. Import Path 2 extends from Oncor’s
           Sand Lake Switch in Ward County to LCRA TSC’s Big Hill Substation in Schleicher
           County to Oncor’s Bell County East Switch in Bell County. The proposed Project is
           the eastern segment of Import Path 2 and consists of (1) an expansion of Oncor’s Bell
           County East Switch to include a 765 kV switching station; (2) a new Bell County East
           Switch – Big Hill Substation 765 kV single-circuit transmission line; and (3)
           telecommunication facilities, including fiber repeater huts, for the operation of the line.

   74.     The Project will improve bi-directional power flow on the ERCOT transmission
           system, increase the reliability of the system, support import capability into the Permian
           Basin region, and support the ability of local transmission networks to serve new loads.

   75.     Staff recommended approval of the Project.

   76.     Applicants demonstrated a reasonable need for the proposed Project.

Project Alternatives
   77.     ERCOT evaluated several transmission-level alternatives to the proposed Project and
           found that none of them more efficiently resolve all the reliability issues identified by
           ERCOT’s analysis.

   78.     The Commission and ERCOT evaluated three alternative import path options—a 345
           kV-, a 500 kV-, and a 765 kV-option. The Commission approved the 765 kV-option,
           which includes this Project. The Commission’s evaluation incorporated information
           received through public workshops, ERCOT working group meetings, formal requests
           for information, and other input from various stakeholders and industry experts
           regarding the carrying capacity, estimated costs, engineering, procurement, and
           construction of the 765 kV alternative relative to the 345 kV and 500 kV options
           presented by ERCOT in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan. Based on the information
           considered and evaluated, the Commission approved the 765 kV option and ordered
           the applicable TSPs to file CCN applications for the identified 765 kV import projects.
           Under the Commission’s order, Applicants are responsible for constructing, operating,
           and maintaining the upgrades included in Applicants’ Application; therefore,
           Applicants did not independently evaluate alternatives.

   79.     The proposed Project is one half of the 765 kV import path identified in the Permian
           Basin Reliability Plan as Import Path 2. The projects recommended in the Permian
           Basin Reliability Plan were the result of months of engagement between ERCOT, the
           Commission, TSPs, and other stakeholders. Through this process, ERCOT evaluated
           alternatives and identified the specific set of transmission system improvements that
           are needed to reliably serve the Permian Basin region. The Commission approved the

                          I.     PROPOSED FINDINGS OF FACT

Joint Applicants
   1.      Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (Oncor) is a Delaware limited liability
           company registered with the Texas secretary of state under filing number 800880712.

   2.      Oncor owns and operates for compensation in Texas facilities and equipment to
           transmit and distribute electricity in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, Inc.
           (ERCOT) region.

   3.      Oncor holds certificate of convenience and necessity (CCN) number 30043 to provide
           service to the public.

    4.     LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (LCRA TSC) is a Texas non-profit
          corporation registered with the Texas secretary of state under filing number
           159084801.
   5.     LCRA TSC owns and operates facilities to transmit electricity in the ERCOT region.

   6.     LCRA TSC provides service under CCN number 30110.

Joint Application
   7.     On March 26, 2026, Oncor and LCRA TSC (Applicants) filed an application
          (Application) with the Public Utility Commission of Texas (Commission) to amend
          their CCNs to (1) expand Oncor's Bell County East Switch to include a 765 kilovolt
          (kV) switchyard, (2) develop a 765 kV transmission line running from LCRA TSC' s
          Big Hill Substation to Oncor's Bell County East Switch, and (3) construct
          telecommunication facilities, including fiber repeater huts, for the operation of the line.

   8.     Applicants hired Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. (Kimley-Horn) and Halff
          Associates, Inc. (Halff) to prepare an environmental assessment and routing study (EA)
          for the proposed transmission line, which was included as part of the Application.

   9.     On April 20, 2026, Commission staff (Staff) recommended that the Application be
          found sufficient.

   10.    In State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) Order No. 7, issued on April 21,
          2026, the administrative law judges (ALJs) found the Application sufficient.

Description of the Transmission Facilities
   11.    Applicants propose to construct, own, and operate a new, single-circuit 765-kV
          transmission line between the expansion at Oncor's Bell County East Switch and
          LCRA TSC's Big Hill Substation. In addition to the transmission line, proposed
          transmission facilities include Oncor' s construction of a new 765-kV switchyard at Bell
          County East Switch and the telecommunications facilities needed to operate the line.

   12.    Oncor' s Bell County East Switch is located 5.5 miles southeast of the city of Temple
          in Bell County.

   13.    LCRA TSC's Big Hill Substation is located approximately 13 miles northeast of the
          City of Eldorado in Schleicher County.

   14.    Except where alternative structures and/or a different right-of-way width is required
          due to design, construction, or other engineering-related constraints, the proposed 765
          kV transmission line will be constructed on single-circuit self-supporting steel lattice
          towers, generally within a 200-foot right-of-way.

   15.     The typical structure will be between approximately 155 and 160 feet in height for
          Oncor' s portion of the transmission line, and between approximately 140-170 feet in
          height for LCRA TSC' s portion of the transmission line, although the actual height

             estimated maximum height for the typical structure will be approximately 198 feet.

Need for the Project
   70.    The proposed transmission facilities are needed to address rapid load growth and help
          ensure the availability ofreliable transmission service in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell,
          Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher,
          Tom Green, and Williamson counties and surrounding areas.

   71.    The proposed Project will establish a new 765-kV transmission pathway that will work
          in conjunction with related upgrades to enhance Applicants' load-serving capability in
          the area.

    72.     On April 24,2025, the Commission approved the 765 kV import paths identified in the
           Permian Basin Reliability Plan and authorized the applicable TSPs to file CCN
           applications for the necessary 765 kV import path projects, as identified by ERCOT.

   73.     The Permian Basin Reliability Plan defined each of the three 765 kV import paths that
           are needed to reliably serve the Permian Basin. Import Path 2 extends from Oncor' s
           Sand Lake Switch in Ward County to LCRA TSC' s Big Hill Substation in Schleicher
           County to Oncor's Bell County East Switch in Bell County. The proposed Project is
           the eastern segment of Import Path 2 and consists of (1) an expansion of Oncor' s Bell
           County East Switch to include a 765 kV switching station; (2) a new Bell County East
           Switch - Big Hill Substation 765 kV single-circuit transmission line; and (3)
           telecommunication facilities, including fiber repeater huts, for the operation of the line.

   74.     The Project will improve bi-directional power flow on the ERCOT transmission
           system, increase the reliability ofthe system, support import capability into the Permian
           Basin region, and support the ability of local transmission networks to serve new loads.

   75.     Staff recommended approval of the Proj ect.

   76.     Applicants demonstrated a reasonable need for the proposed Proj ect.

Project Alternatives
   77.     ERCOT evaluated several transmission-level alternatives to the proposed Project and
           found that none of them more efficiently resolve all the reliability issues identified by
           ERCOT's analysis.

   78.     The Commission and ERCOT evaluated three alternative import path options-a 345
           kV-, a 500 kV-, and a 765 kV-option. The Commission approved the 765 kV-option,
           which includes this Project. The Commission' s evaluation incorporated information
           received through public workshops, ERCOT working group meetings, formal requests
           for information, and other input from various stakeholders and industry experts
           regarding the carrying capacity, estimated costs, engineering, procurement, and
           construction of the 765 kV alternative relative to the 345 kV and 500 kV options
           presented by ERCOT in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan. Based on the information
           considered and evaluated, the Commission approved the 765 kV option and ordered
           the applicable TSPs to file CCN applications for the identified 765 kV import projects.
           Under the Commission' s order, Applicants are responsible for constructing, operating,
           and maintaining the upgrades included in Applicants' Application; therefore,
           Applicants did not independently evaluate alternatives.

   79.     The proposed Project is one half of the 765 kV import path identified in the Permian
           Basin Reliability Plan as Import Path 2. The projects recommended in the Permian
           Basin Reliability Plan were the result of months of engagement between ERCOT, the
           Commission, TSPs, and other stakeholders. Through this process, ERCOT evaluated
           alternatives and identified the specific set of transmission system improvements that
           are needed to reliably serve the Permian Basin region. The Commission approved the
